common.tagline: Understand how things change, on your terms.
common.notDiagnosis: Not a diagnosis. Masar shows direction of change and what is still unknown; it never gives a fertility score.
common.demoBadge: Prototype with synthetic people. Nothing here is real patient data.

hint.Education: General information. Nothing here is about you specifically.
hint.DecisionSupport: Your own information explained, with options listed neutrally. No recommendation of one option.
hint.ClinicianOnly: Interpretation and decisions stay with a qualified clinician.

directions.Unknown: Not enough data for a trend

hint.Improving: Supportive factors have moved in a helpful direction since the previous reading.
hint.Stable: Little change between readings. Stable is not the same as 'all clear'.
hint.Shifting: Something has changed between readings. Shifting is a reason to look closer, not an alarm.
hint.Discuss: A pattern here is worth a conversation with a clinician. It is not a diagnosis.
hint.Unknown: We can't speak to this yet. Adding information would help.

confidence.label: What this is based on
confidence.notEnoughHint: There are no usable readings for this area, so Masar does not name a direction. It is not calling this stable, and it is not calling it a concern.

hint.High: Several recent readings, including the ones that matter most for this area.
hint.Moderate: A few recent readings. Enough to see a direction, not detail.
hint.Low: One reading, or only older ones.
hint.InsufficientData: No readings for this area. Nothing can be said about direction.

hint.NotPlanning: You'll see education and what would help us see more. No pressure to act.
hint.MaybeLater: Timing matters here, so age and reserve context are surfaced gently.
hint.Pregnant: Wellbeing in pregnancy and any condition follow-up are prioritised.
hint.PreferNotToSay: You'll see everything as general information.

about.cycle: How regular your cycles are and what influences them.
about.reserve: Age and, where available, lab context about the quantity of remaining eggs. Never quality.
about.metabolic: Weight trend, blood sugar, blood pressure and activity.
about.male: Semen analysis where available, and the everyday factors associated with it.
about.conditions: Conditions and family history you've recorded that can be relevant.
about.lifestyle: Sleep, movement, smoking, stress, laughter and connection, from your check-ins.

factors.family_male_infertility_family: Male fertility difficulty in the family

driverNotes.pcos_features_modifiable: The condition itself is not a choice, but several of its features respond to lifestyle.
driverNotes.amh_quantity_not_quality: Reflects approximate quantity of eggs, not quality. A weak predictor of natural conception.
driverNotes.semen_varies_between_samples: Results vary between samples; one value is never a verdict.
driverNotes.health_age_simulated: Simulated Health Age tile; a real deployment would read the programme's value.

missing.amh: An AMH result, for discussion with a clinician
missing.heat_exposure: Whether your routine involves heat exposure

summaries.cycle_improving: Cycles settling is encouraging. Keep recording dates so the view stays clear.
summaries.cycle_stable: Regular cycles are one piece of context among many. They don't confirm ovulation or fertility.
summaries.cycle_shifting: Cycle changes have many causes: stress, thyroid, weight change, PCOS, travel. If it persists, it's worth a conversation.
summaries.cycle_discuss: A persistent change or a relevant condition makes this worth discussing with a clinician. It is not a diagnosis.
summaries.cycle_unknown: We can't speak to cycle health yet. Three months of dates would change that.
summaries.reserve_improving: Reserve context doesn't improve in a biological sense; a clearer view may simply reveal more than expected.
summaries.reserve_stable: AMH in the typical range is context, not reassurance about conceiving. Quantity, not quality.
summaries.reserve_shifting: A noticeable fall between results is worth understanding in context with a clinician.
summaries.reserve_discuss: Either a lower AMH, a family history or your age and plans make a conversation about timing useful.
summaries.reserve_unknown: Age alone describes a population trend, not your reserve. A lab result would narrow this, if you want one.
summaries.reserve_single_lab: One AMH result is context, not a direction. It reflects quantity, not quality, and a second result over time is what would show change.
summaries.metabolic_improving: A helpful metabolic direction supports ovulation and semen health in general evidence.
summaries.metabolic_stable: Steady readings. Stable is a description, not a judgement.
summaries.metabolic_shifting: A change in weight or blood sugar is modifiable context, and worth a look.
summaries.metabolic_discuss: A reading sits in a range clinicians like to review, especially around pregnancy plans.
summaries.metabolic_unknown: We can't see a metabolic direction yet. Two readings over time are needed.
summaries.male_improving: Stopping smoking is associated with better semen parameters within a few months.
summaries.male_stable: Values within reference limits are context, not a guarantee.
summaries.male_shifting: Smoking plus a higher BMI are modifiable factors associated with semen changes.
summaries.male_discuss: A value below the reference limit is common and often repeated; a clinician can interpret it in context.
summaries.male_unknown: Without a semen analysis, male factor stays in shade. That is a normal place to be.
summaries.conditions_stable: What you've recorded isn't changing. Keep it current.
summaries.conditions_shifting: Something has changed in your recorded history.
summaries.conditions_discuss: A recorded condition or family history is relevant to your plans and worth discussing.
summaries.conditions_unknown: Completing the conditions step would change what we can say.
summaries.lifestyle_improving: More supportive habits than before. Small and repeatable beats dramatic.
summaries.lifestyle_stable: Steady habits. Nothing to fix for its own sake.
summaries.lifestyle_shifting: Fewer supportive habits recently. Life happens; this is a nudge, not a mark.
summaries.lifestyle_discuss: Very high stress deserves support in its own right.
summaries.lifestyle_unknown: A second check-in would let us see a direction.

welcome.title: Understand how things change, on your terms.
welcome.subtitle: Masar watches the direction of change in reproductive health, explains it plainly, and helps you decide what, if anything, to do next.

pillars.directionBody: Each area shows whether things are improving, stable, shifting or worth discussing, and how much we can actually see.
pillars.honestBody: When information is missing we say so, and tell you what would narrow it.
pillars.yoursBody: Every source and every recipient is a switch you control, with a log you can read.

about.title: How Masar decides what to show
about.subtitle: Every threshold is written here in plain language. Rules compute. Humans advise. AI, where used, only rephrases approved text.
refused: A fertility score or pregnancy probability.
A chatbot that answers medical questions freely.
Any pathway for employers, insurers or marketing to see data.
A claim that this is validated or connected to real health records.

rules.r0_no_score: Masar never sums areas into a number. Each area has a direction and how much we can see, nothing more.
rules.r1_confidence: Visibility: no readings means 'mostly in shade'; only old readings means 'faint'; two or more recent readings means 'partial'; four or more recent readings including the key one means 'clear'. Labs count as recent for 12 months, cycle dates for 6, check-ins for 3.
rules.r2_guard: If an area has almost no recorded information, it can never be shown as 'Stable'. It is shown as 'Not enough data for a trend'.
rules.c1_regularity: Cycles are called irregular when any is shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days, or when the spread of the last three exceeds 7 days.
rules.c2_persistent: Irregular recent cycles after irregular earlier cycles (more than three months) are 'worth discussing'. Irregular after regular is 'shifting'. Regular after irregular is 'improving'.
rules.c3_amenorrhoea: No period for 90 days or more is 'worth discussing'.
rules.c4_conditions: PCOS, endometriosis or a thyroid condition together with an intention of trying or maybe-later makes cycle health 'worth discussing'.
rules.o1_age_only: Without AMH, antral follicle count or FSH, reserve is 'can't say yet'. Age is shown as context only.
rules.o2_amh: AMH below 1.0 ng/mL is 'worth discussing' as a reference for conversation, not a diagnosis. A fall of 25% or more between two results within 24 months is 'shifting'. A single typical result is reported as observed but is not called 'stable': direction needs two results.
rules.o3_preserve: Age 35 or older, intention maybe-later and no reserve results suggests a preservation discussion, never a recommendation.
rules.m1_bmi_trend: A BMI change of 1.0 or more between readings at least six months apart sets the direction (down from 25+ is improving, up is shifting).
rules.m2_hba1c: HbA1c of 6.5% or more, or 5.7% or more with pregnancy plans, is 'worth discussing'. A fall of 0.3 or more is 'improving'.
rules.a1_semen: Any semen value below the WHO 2021 reference (concentration 16 M/mL, motility 42%, volume 1.4 mL) is 'worth discussing'. Within limits is 'stable'.
rules.a2_lifestyle: Without a semen analysis, current smoking plus BMI 30 or more is 'shifting'; stopping smoking is 'improving'; otherwise 'can't say yet'.
rules.k1_intention: A recorded condition with an intention of trying or maybe-later is 'worth discussing'.
rules.k2_pregnant: A recorded condition during pregnancy is 'worth discussing' promptly.
rules.l1_supportive: Each check-in counts supportive habits: sleep 7 to 9 hours, 150+ minutes of activity, not currently smoking, low alcohol, stress under 6, laughter or connection on 3+ days. One more than last time is 'improving', one fewer is 'shifting'.
rules.l2_distress: Stress of 8 or more is 'worth discussing' and surfaces wellbeing support.

metabolic.whatIsBody: Metabolic health describes how the body manages processes such as blood sugar and blood pressure. Weight trends and physical activity can provide additional context. These factors may inform broader health discussions, but they do not independently determine fertility.
metabolic.noScore: Nothing here is combined into a score. Four separate readings, each with its own date.

weight.title: Weight trend
weight.body: Body mass index over time. One reading is a snapshot; two or more, months apart, show a trend.

sugar.title: Blood sugar
sugar.body: HbA1c, an average of blood sugar over about three months. Usually from a laboratory.

pressure.title: Blood pressure
pressure.body: The top (systolic) number from a blood pressure reading, at a clinic or at home.

activity.title: Physical activity
activity.body: Minutes of moderate activity in a typical week, from a check-in or a connected device.

statusHint.available: Two or more readings in range. A direction can be seen.
statusHint.single: One recent reading. A direction needs a second one over time.
statusHint.outdated: The latest reading is more than {months} months old, so it no longer counts towards direction.
statusHint.missing: Nothing recorded yet. Nothing can be said about this.

metabolic.connect: Or switch on a record source

emptyState.connectOne: One record source is switched off
emptyState.import: Import a simulated record or lab result
emptyState.footnote: Every link here opens a screen that really records that information. Nothing is added to your record until you save it.

timeline.title: Your health story, over time
timeline.body: What was already recorded, what arrived recently, and the moments Masar's reading of this area actually changed. Older readings are marked so they are not mistaken for current ones.
timeline.noTrend: A trend cannot be established yet. It takes at least two comparable readings, months apart, to see a direction.
timeline.noChange: The reading of this area has not changed across these snapshots. New information was added, but it did not move the picture.
timeline.empty: Nothing recorded for this area yet.

demo.label: Guided demo
demo.title: One journey. Better-informed decisions.
demo.subtitle: Meet Fatima and Mariam. See how the same health platform responds differently depending on what each person has shared, and how one new piece of information can change the picture.
demo.problem: Most reproductive-health tools hand people a score. Masar does something quieter: it shows what has changed, how clearly it can be seen, and what would help see more. Nothing is called stable without evidence, and nothing leaves a person's record without their say.
demo.meet: Meet the people in this story

fatima.name: Fatima
fatima.line: 28 · not planning for now · has shared very little so far
fatima.body: Fatima has told Masar her age, one cycle length and how she is feeling this month. She has not connected any records or lab results, and her clinician access is switched off. Her story shows what honest looks like when there is almost nothing to go on.

mariam.name: Mariam
mariam.line: 33 · maybe in a few years · living with PCOS
mariam.body: Mariam has eighteen months of cycle notes, simulated health-record readings of weight and blood pressure, an older HbA1c and a Health Age tile. Her cycles have moved from regular to irregular. Her clinician, partner and population analytics are all switched on. Her story shows what changes when there is a history to compare against.

personas.also: Also in the story: Dr Layla, who reviews Mariam's screen, and Sara, who reads Masar in Arabic.

demo.startHint: Each chapter signs you in as the right person and opens the real screen. A slim guide at the bottom tells you what to notice.
demo.doneBody: Fatima saw what was missing and how to add it. Mariam saw a real change, added one result, asked for a conversation, let a clinician in and then closed the door. Sara read all of it in Arabic. Nothing on those screens was a score, and nothing was shown without consent.
demo.exploreBody: Open any screen on its own, outside the story.

explore.mariamPrivacy: Mariam's data settings and access log
explore.howItWorks: How it works and what we refused to build

demo.synthetic: Everyone in this demo is synthetic. Fatima, Mariam, Omar, Sara and Dr Layla are invented people with invented records. No real patient data is used anywhere, and no real laboratory or health-record system is contacted.
demo.resetHint: Puts Fatima, Mariam, Omar and Sara back to their starting point. The population cohort is untouched.
demo.resetConfirm: Reset the four demo people to their seeded state?

importCard.title: A new lab result arrives
importCard.body: Mariam has no egg-reserve lab context yet. Pressing the button writes one simulated AMH result through the same path a connected laboratory would use, then recomputes her view.
importCard.bodyHas: Mariam's record already holds one simulated AMH result, added during this demo. Pressing the button again adds nothing: the same reading on the same day is never written twice.
importCard.already: This result is already in Mariam's record. Nothing was added a second time.
importCard.blocked: Mariam has lab results switched off, so nothing was written. The blocked attempt is in her access log.
importCard.whatAddsBody: A first lab reading for egg-reserve context, with a date and reference range. The area moves from unseen to faintly seen, the value is reported as observed, and the explanation below now mentions it.
importCard.cannotBody: One AMH reading is not a trend, says nothing about egg quality, and is not a fertility score. A second reading over time is what would show direction.
importCard.persisted: This result is saved. It stays in Mariam's record until the demo is reset.
importCard.noteStatic: Add the result to see the before and after.

import.title: Import synthetic data
import.body: Simulated connectors. Each button writes a FHIR-shaped synthetic observation if that source is switched on in your data settings.
import.device_sleep: Device: a week of sleep and activity
import.blocked: Blocked: {source} is switched off. The block was logged.
import.duplicate: Already in your record today from {source}. Nothing was added twice.

footer.disclaimer: Masar is a hackathon prototype using synthetic people. It is not clinically validated, not a medical device, and not connected to Malaffi, Health Age or any real record system.

account.demoBanner: Synthetic people only. No real health records are connected.

dashboard.headline: Understand your health. Decide what comes next.
dashboard.subheadline: A personal view of your recorded information, what has changed, and what may be worth discussing.

hero.title: Your trajectory
hero.tagline: A longitudinal view of what has changed — direction and confidence per area, never a fertility score.

radar.label: Your areas at a glance
radar.hint: Tap an area to open its trajectory below.

context.label: Patient context
context.syntheticNotice: Synthetic demonstration profile. No real patient data.

trajectory.title: Your health trajectory
trajectory.subtitle: A chronological view of recorded observations—not a prediction of fertility.
trajectory.measuredVsInterpreted: Readings are what was recorded, with date and source. The summary is how Masar's readable rules describe them. A new reading does not always change the summary.
trajectory.cycleEarlier: The three cycles before the latest three

cmp.single: Only one reading is recorded, so no comparison is possible.
cmp.tooClose: The two latest readings are {days} days apart. Masar does not compare readings less than a week apart.
cmp.same: Same value as the earlier reading, {days} days apart.
cmp.delta: {change} compared with the earlier reading, {days} days apart.
cmp.textSame: Same answer as the earlier reading.
cmp.previousOutdated: The earlier reading is older than its freshness window.
cmp.cycleFew: Cycle dates recorded: {n}. At least three are needed before Masar describes a pattern.
cmp.cycleNoEarlier: There is no earlier set of three cycles, so Masar cannot compare recent cycles with earlier ones.
cmp.cycleSets: Average of the latest three: {recent} days. Average of the three before: {earlier} days.
cmp.disclaimer: A difference between two readings is a fact about the record, not a judgement. Whether it matters is a clinical question.

trajectory.nothingRecorded: Nothing is recorded in this area yet.
trajectory.nothingRecordedBody: There is nothing to compare, and Masar does not fill the gap with an assumption.
trajectory.noChartBody: A chart needs at least two readings of the same measure, a week or more apart. Fewer would draw a line the records do not support.
trajectory.cannotNoReadings: Nothing here is recorded, so no change over time can be described.
trajectory.cannotNoComparison: No measure in this area has two readings a week or more apart, so no change over time can be shown.
trajectory.cannotPredict: Masar describes recorded information only. It does not predict outcomes or what will happen next.
trajectory.interpretationNote: These are recalculated summaries, not new measurements.
trajectory.noInterpretation: No summary has been stored for this area yet.
trajectory.noChangeSince: Masar's reading of this area has not changed since.
trajectory.oneMeasurement: One measurement recorded ({date}). A trend needs at least two readings, a week or more apart.
trajectory.detailsHint: Every recorded reading, how it compares with the one before, and how Masar's summary changed.

reason.time: A reading passed its freshness window

insights.title: What deserves your attention
insights.subtitle: The most relevant point from your records, and what it can and cannot tell you.
insights.discussFlagged: Recorded: {items}. A clinician can read this alongside your full history. This is not a diagnosis.
insights.discussDirection: This may be worth raising at an appointment if it continues or concerns you. A clinician can read it alongside your full history; Masar does not diagnose.
insights.noRecordsUsed: No recorded values feed this insight.
insights.noneYetBody: There isn't enough recorded information to point to anything specific. Adding a few items would help.
insights.noInfoBody: For these areas there are no usable measurements, so no trend or conclusion is shown.
insights.metabolicEmpty: Not enough information yet. We don't have recorded measurements to identify a trend.
insights.genericEmpty: Not enough information yet. We don't have enough recorded observations in this area to identify a trend.

cannotByDomain.cycle: Cycle patterns alone do not confirm ovulation, egg quality, or pregnancy potential, and do not establish a medical diagnosis.
cannotByDomain.reserve: AMH and age cannot measure egg quality, predict natural conception, or establish fertility status on their own.
cannotByDomain.metabolic: Weight, blood sugar, blood pressure, and activity provide general health context; they do not independently determine fertility.
cannotByDomain.male: A single semen or lifestyle observation does not establish male fertility status; parameters vary between samples and require clinical review.
cannotByDomain.conditions: Recorded conditions indicate topics for clinical review; they are not a fertility prognosis or autonomous clinical advice.
cannotByDomain.lifestyle: Self-reported sleep, stress, smoking, and activity describe modifiable wellbeing context, not a clinical fertility measurement.

connections.title: How your information connects
connections.subtitle: Recorded items that are relevant together in a clinical conversation. Masar does not conclude that one causes another.
connections.caution: These associations are for discussion with a clinician. Masar does not conclude cause and effect, and nothing here is a diagnosis.

condition_cycle.title: A recorded condition and a cycle pattern
condition_cycle.body: You have a recorded condition that can relate to cycles, and your recent cycles are flagged. They are relevant together in a clinical conversation; the records do not show that one explains the other.

metabolic_cycle.title: Metabolic readings and your cycles
metabolic_cycle.body: Some metabolic readings and your cycle pattern are both flagged. Clinicians often look at them together; the records here cannot show that either one is behind the other.

planning_timing.title: Your plans and the areas flagged
planning_timing.body: Your recorded goal is to plan a pregnancy now or later, and at least one area is marked for discussion. A clinician can weigh timing against your history; Masar does not set a timeline.

male_metabolic.title: Semen results and metabolic readings
male_metabolic.body: A semen-related result and some metabolic readings are both flagged. They are relevant together in a conversation; this record cannot show that one causes the other.

reserve_context.title: A reserve result next to other flagged areas
reserve_context.body: A recorded AMH result sits next to other flagged areas. AMH reflects approximate egg quantity, not quality, and cannot on its own explain the other findings.

steps.title: Your next step
steps.subtitle: One or two things worth doing now, why they are offered, and where each one stands.
steps.pathwayBody: Each step shows only what has actually been recorded, with its date.
steps.noPathway: No consultation or counselling step has been suggested from your current record.

complete.title: Complete your health profile
complete.body: Adding these would let Masar describe more: {items}.

review.title: Review a recorded result
review.body: {factor}: {value} (recorded {date}) sits under “{area}”, which Masar marks “{direction}”. Open it to see what it does and does not show.

prepare.title: Prepare questions for a clinician
prepare.body: Copy questions from Living Well into one list to bring to an appointment. The list is saved on this device only.

learn.title: Read about a factor you can influence
learn.body: {title}. Evidence is labelled, and nothing here asks you to decide.

steps.noneTitle: No action is justified by your current record
steps.noneBody: Masar does not suggest counselling or referral without supporting evidence. You can add information to your profile or read the education hubs.
steps.reviewsNone: No clinician has recorded a review of your summary.
steps.reviewsHint: Recorded under the clinician's name, not by Masar.
steps.more: {n} more on the Next steps page

next.Suggested: This was suggested from your recorded information. Nothing has been sent to anyone. Choose Request to save your request.
next.Requested: Your request is saved in your record. This prototype books no appointment and sends no message. Mark it confirmed once you have a time.
next.Confirmed: You marked this as confirmed. After the appointment, mark it attended.
next.Attended: Marked as attended. Record what happened to keep a follow-up in your record.
next.OutcomeRecorded: Follow-up recorded. This pathway is complete.
next.Declined: You chose not now. Nothing was sent. Masar can suggest it again if your record changes.
next.Expired: This step is no longer suggested by your current record.

card.title: By area
card.subtitle: Each area shows what is recorded, what that does and does not mean, and the next step.
card.reserveNotAssessed: Masar has not assessed egg reserve. Age alone is not a measurement of it.
card.cycleDates: Cycle dates recorded: {n}. Within the last six months: {recent}.
card.cycleFew: Three recent cycle dates are needed before Masar describes a pattern.

overview.title: What we know so far
overview.summary: {n} recorded observations. The most recent is from {date}.
overview.relevanceNote: General health indicators such as weight, blood sugar, blood pressure, sleep and activity do not predict fertility on their own. Masar shows them only as background for a conversation with a clinician.

goalBody.NotPlanning: You are not planning a pregnancy right now. Masar can help you keep track of your recorded information and understand what may be worth raising at a routine appointment.
goalBody.MaybeLater: You may plan a pregnancy in the next few years. Masar can help you see how your recorded information relates to that question and what to prepare for a conversation with a clinician.
goalBody.TryingNow: You are trying for a pregnancy now. Masar can help you prepare for a conversation with a clinician about what your recorded information does and does not show.
goalBody.Pregnant: You are pregnant. Masar focuses on wellbeing, follow-up of any recorded conditions, and questions to bring to your care team.
goalBody.PreferNotToSay: You have chosen not to share a goal. Masar shows general information about your records and keeps its suggestions neutral.

details.title: Your information in detail
details.subtitle: Everything recorded, grouped by how closely it relates to reproductive health.

reproductive.title: Reproductive health records
reproductive.body: Cycle dates, laboratory results and semen analysis are the most direct information.

history.title: Medical history
history.body: Conditions and family history a clinician may want to consider.

context.title: General health context
context.body: Weight, blood sugar, blood pressure, sleep and activity. These do not predict fertility on their own, but they can matter for a conversation about your health.

summary.readWatch: {n} areas are worth a closer look
summary.readWatchOne: One area is worth a closer look
summary.readCalm: Nothing in your records needs attention right now
summary.readNone: Masar needs a little more information first
summary.readBody: Based only on what you chose to share. Masar describes direction of change over time — never a fertility score or a diagnosis.
summary.noNextStep: No clinical step is open. Keep adding readings so change can be seen early.
summary.allAreasSub: Direction of change, and how much information sits behind it.
summary.readPartial: Too little is recorded yet to call anything settled

forbidden.title: This workspace is not available to you
forbidden.body: You are signed in, but this area is for a different role. Patient, clinician and health-system views are kept separate. Access is checked on the server, not only by hiding a menu item.

roles.subtitle: This demonstration uses synthetic people. Pick a path that matches the role you want to explore.
roles.seededHint: Seeded story personas remain available from Demo sign-in if judges need a fixed case.

clinician.body: Guidelines consent, then the authorised patient review workspace.

admin.body: Guidelines consent, then aggregate pathway and equity metrics.

consent.title: Before we continue
consent.subtitle: Masar only uses what you agree to share. You can change your mind later in Your data.
consent.declineHint: If you decline, you return to the start. Nothing is stored against a new journey until you accept.

points.guidelines: You are reviewing a prototype. It is not a medical device and does not replace clinical care.
points.synthetic: All people and records in this demo are synthetic. No real Abu Dhabi health records are connected.
points.control: Consent is granular and revocable. Reproductive information is not used for employment or insurance.
points.share: Continuing allows Masar to store the answers you choose to give for your personal view.

stepper.optional: Every question is optional. Skip anything you prefer not to answer.

titles.labs: Laboratory results you may already have

bodies.intention: This shapes which options appear later. It is not a fertility label.
bodies.cycle: Choose a pattern that roughly matches recent cycles, or skip.
bodies.conditions: Select anything that applies, or prefer not to say.
bodies.lifestyle: A rough picture of sleep, movement and stress is enough.
bodies.labs: Optional illustrative values for the demo. Discuss real results with a clinician.
bodies.medications: Optional. Skip if you prefer not to list medicines.

stepper.labsHint: Selecting an option adds a synthetic reading for this demonstration only.

prepare.title: Preparing your view
prepare.body: Masar is arranging what you shared into a longitudinal picture—direction of change, not a one-off label.
prepare.hint: This usually takes a few seconds.
prepare.aria: Quiet pulse while your view is prepared

ai.title: May we use Claude for plain-language wording?
ai.subtitle: Direction of change still comes from readable rules. Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, only helps phrase what those rules already found—if you allow it.
ai.noKey: No Claude API key is configured on this server. You can still continue; wording will use Masar’s built-in text.

points.rules: Rules compute direction, confidence and what is still unknown.
points.model: Claude may rephrase approved text into shorter plain language. It does not invent numbers, and anything it writes is checked before you see it.
points.noScore: Masar never produces a fertility score or diagnosis.
points.decline: If you decline, you still see your dashboard with Masar’s standard explanations.

rail.title: Your first visit
rail.subtitle: About five minutes. Every question is optional, and you can change any answer later.
rail.privacy: Nothing here is shared with employers or insurers. There is no setting that allows it.

bio.heroImageAlt: Soft natural light across a calm interior space
bio.heroTitle: See change earlier. Decide with clarity.
bio.heroBody: Masar watches the direction of your reproductive health over time—not a score, not a verdict—so options stay personal, calm and in your control.
bio.privacyLine: You choose what is shared. Employment and insurance are never purposes.
bio.signalsTitle: Direction, confidence, and what is still unknown
bio.signalsBody: Each area of your health shows how things are moving, how sure Masar can be, and what would narrow the picture—never a fertility label.

direction.title: Direction of change
direction.body: Improving, stable, shifting, or worth discussing—with the date and source beside every reading.

confidence.title: Honest confidence
confidence.body: High, moderate, low, or not enough information. Missing data is never called stable.

consent.title: Consent you can revoke
consent.body: Share by purpose. There is no setting for employers, insurers or marketing apps.

cycle.label: Cycle health
cycle.note: Three recent cycle lengths would clarify the pattern.

metabolic.label: Metabolic health
metabolic.note: A recent HbA1c would narrow this conversation.

unknown.label: Egg reserve context
unknown.note: An AMH result is for discussion with a clinician—not a verdict.

bio.timelineTitle: From a quiet signal to a timely conversation
bio.timelineBody: Masar holds the thread between what is recorded and what may be worth discussing—without rushing you.

signal.title: A signal appears
signal.body: Something in your records shifts—or stays missing. Masar surfaces it with context, not alarms.

pattern.title: The pattern holds or changes
pattern.body: Direction and confidence update as new readings arrive. Uncertainty stays visible.

option.title: Options, not prescriptions
option.body: Intention-aware choices are listed neutrally—learn, optimise, discuss tests, or speak with a clinician.

counsel.title: A clinician keeps the decision
counsel.body: When discussion is warranted, Masar routes you toward care. Software never substitutes clinical advice.

evidence.title: Rules compute. Humans advise.
evidence.body: Readable rules decide direction. Optional wording help never invents numbers or diagnoses.

bio.enterTitle: Choose how you want to enter
bio.enterBody: This demonstration uses synthetic people. Pick a path that matches the role you want to explore.
bio.photoCredit: Photography is illustrative and does not depict real patients.

v2.pill: Abu Dhabi reproductive-health prototype · synthetic data
v2.h1a: Know how your reproductive health is changing
v2.lede: Masar turns scattered records — cycles, labs, history, lifestyle — into a clear view of change over time, explains what it can and cannot tell you, and routes you to the right conversation early. Never a fertility score.

facts.l: minimum group size in population views

v2.bentoTitle: From scattered signals to a timely, informed choice

trajectory.b: Every area shows its direction across dates. Masar separates real change from normal variation and says when there is too little to tell.

evidence.b: What was recorded, why it may matter, the evidence behind it, and what it cannot tell you.

action.b: Learn, optimise, discuss testing, counselling, preservation or referral, tracked until it happens.

consent.t: Consent you can see and revoke
consent.b: Switch each source and each recipient on or off. Every access is logged.

clinician.b: Trends, gaps and the reasons behind each flag. The clinician accepts, modifies or overrides.

population.b: Uptake, time to counselling and equity of reach, with small groups suppressed.

mock.mattersV: A noticeable fall is worth discussing in context.
mock.cannotV: Egg quality or chance of conception.

v2.journeyTitle: Six steps from first visit to clinical follow-up

journey.b: Choose what to share, source by source.
Factors, evidence and what is missing.

v2.privacyTitle: Reproductive data is never for employers, insurers or marketing.
v2.privacyBody: Not a policy setting. There is no code path that grants those purposes, and every attempt to read your data is written to a log you can see.
privacyItems: Granular consent per source and recipient

Audit log of every view, share and block
